elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Inserted §5.5: "The Company shall own all work product created for the Company under this Agreement, including the Site and its code, design and look and feel (the \"Deliverables\")" — ownership vests in the Customer and the Deliverables term is defined in the same sentence.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "HDI hereby assigns all right, title and interest in the Deliverables to the Company" — present-tense assignment running from Vendor to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any HDI intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables" — perpetual, and scoped to embedded Vendor IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: §5.5: licence is expressly "royalty-free"; no fee or offset condition attached.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: §5.5: "The Company retains all rights in the Content and in all user, customer and order data generated through the Site" — tracks the data actually held under §2.1/§8.1 using the Agreement's own "Content" term rather than an undefined "Customer Data".

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §5.5 final sentence: "The Parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property." §10.2's "co-ownership" reference concerns the parties' relationship, not IP, so no contradiction arises.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: §5.5 "HDI retains its pre-existing intellectual property" preserves Vendor ownership of its pre-existing tools; nothing in the insertion sweeps Vendor know-how into the assignment beyond work product created for the Company.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The insertion vests outright ownership of the Deliverables in the Company rather than granting the Company a licence to them; no Deliverables licence (perpetual or otherwise) is rendered. Ownership is stronger than the fallback, but the fallback element is not literally present.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No licence to Deliverables is granted at all — only a licence to HDI IP embedded in the Deliverables — so no irrevocability term for a Deliverables licence exists.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence is granted; the embedded-IP licence in §5.5 also omits the word "worldwide".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence is granted; §5.5 instead assigns title to the Company.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No express use/modify licence language; these rights follow from the assignment of all right, title and interest rather than from a rendered licence grant.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing language appears; the fallback licence architecture was not used.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Duplicate element listing: as above, the redline uses assignment/ownership, not a Deliverables licence.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: nothing in the original text (§1.1, §5.2, §5.3, §6.1, §10.2) allocates ownership of the Site, its code and look and feel, or of the data the Site generates.

All eight preferred elements are met by the single inserted §5.5 in operative language: Customer ownership of work product including the Site, present-tense assignment by HDI, HDI retention of pre-existing IP, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded HDI IP, Customer retention of all rights in Content and user/customer/order data, and an express no-joint-ownership sentence.

The fallback level is not satisfied on its literal terms because the redline uses assignment rather than a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence with use/modify/sublicense rights; this is immaterial since the preferred level is complete and ownership is more favourable to us than the fallback licence.

Minimal: one concise new clause, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or indemnity add-ons, no procedures, and no favourable existing language deleted or duplicated. §5.2 (artistic and editorial control), §5.3 (title to physical Deerskin Products) and §6.1 (trademark licence to HDI) are left intact.

Preserves intent: the insertion uses the Agreement's existing "Content" and "Site" terms, defines "Deliverables" in place, creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict §10.2's non-IP "co-ownership" language.

Note for the drafter (not a defect at the preferred level): the embedded-IP licence omits "worldwide" and sublicensing rights; if HDI pushes back to a licence-only structure, those words must be added to reach the fallback.
